description: The United States and Israel launched joint air strikes on Iran, starting the 2026 Iran war. Strait of Hormuz tanker traffic ground to a near halt in the following days.
China, India, Japan and South Korea account for 75% of oil and 59% of LNG exports from the Strait of Hormuz region, per pre-war analysis of Asian exposure to a potential Hormuz disruption.
Brent crude oil prices surged 10-13% to around $80-82 per barrel.

Qatar's Ministry of Defence announced two Iranian drones attacked Qatari gas facilities; QatarEnergy announced all gas production in the country had been halted. European natural gas prices nearly doubled.
US petrol prices began rising 5-10 cents per gallon daily as the war began; the US, buffered by domestic production, faced comparatively less direct impact.
Japanese PM Takaichi stated Japan retains 254 days' worth of oil reserves amid the Strait of Hormuz closure.
QatarEnergy announced it was declaring Force Majeure on its contracts with buyers, and would soon shut down gas liquefaction as LNG tankers could not leave the Gulf.
EU natural gas prices decreased to a less-high €48/MWh on Wednesday 4 March, after the initial spike from the Qatar attack.
Analysts warned UK household energy bills could rise by £160 after the Iran conflict pushed gas prices higher.

event: China halts new fuel export contracts
description: China ordered major refiners including Sinopec and Rongsheng Petrochemical to stop accepting new fuel export contracts; jet fuel refuelling for international flights and supplies to Hong Kong/Macau were exempted.
Indian refiners began buying prompt Russian oil as the Iran war disrupted Middle East supplies.
Qatar warned that if the war continued, other Gulf energy producers might be forced to halt exports and declare Force Majeure.
Satellite imagery analysis by Bloomberg and Tokyo's Energy Economics and Society Research Institute showed Qatar's Ras Laffan gas facility appeared undamaged before its 'unprecedented shutdown'.
Universities were closed early ahead of Eid al-Fitr holidays to conserve electricity and fuel.

event: India readies coal power for summer
description: India said it was ready for unprecedented coal power demand in summer amid the oil and gas crisis, with adequate coal stock for 88 days.

event: IEA agrees historic 400 mb emergency release
description: IEA member countries unanimously agreed to make 400 mb of oil from emergency reserves available to the market to address war-related disruptions.

event: IEA: largest oil supply disruption in history
description: IEA Oil Market Report (12 March 2026): the war is creating 'the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market'. Crude/product flows through Hormuz plunged from ~20 mb/d pre-war to a trickle; Gulf countries cut oil production by at least 10 mb/d; global oil supply projected to plunge 8 mb/d in March; Brent traded within a whisker of $120/bbl before easing to ~$92/bbl, up $20/bbl for the month.

event: NZ releases 6 days of fuel reserves
description: New Zealand released six days' worth of petroleum reserves following a global IEA directive to release 400 million barrels in response to supply disruptions.
Nepal Oil Corporation announced that, as of 13 March, authorities would refill only half of consumers' empty LPG cylinders to lengthen stockpiles.
Southeast Asian governments and businesses began shutting offices and limiting travel as the oil crisis deepened.

event: NYT: possibly the largest oil shock ever
description: Article draws parallels between the crisis and the 1970s oil shocks, describing echoes of that era in what may now be the largest oil shock ever.
A surge in oil prices shakes Pakistan's already fragile economy.
The Government of Japan began releasing 80 million barrels of oil, equivalent to 15 days of domestic demand, from its strategic reserves.

event: Iran attacks Ras Laffan LNG complex
description: Iran hit Qatar's inactive Ras Laffan Industrial City LNG complex, causing a 17% reduction in Qatar's LNG production capacity. Damage was estimated to take 3-5 years to fix. LNG spot prices in Asia subsequently increased by over 140%.
China's large strategic petroleum reserves, built up over years, helped insulate the country significantly from the war and the ensuing global fuel crisis.
Slovenia became the first EU country to introduce fuel rationing since the crisis began, limiting purchases to 50 litres/day for private motorists and 200 litres/day for businesses and farmers.
The Philippines declared a state of emergency, driven partly by a concurrent strike by transport workers amid the energy crisis.

event: China dials back fuel price hikes
description: The Chinese government reduced its planned fuel price hikes to 'reduce burden' on drivers, after queues formed at gas stations in multiple Chinese cities.
The New Zealand Government announced that about 143,000 working families with children would receive a $50 tax credit to help with rising fuel costs, effective 7 April.
Australia holds around 29 to 36 days' worth of fuel reserves.

event: Shell CEO warns of European shortage
description: Shell's CEO warned that Europe could face fuel shortages by April if Iran continued to throttle supplies.

event: EU urges early gas storage filling
description: The European Commission advised member states to fill their gas storages early to avoid price spikes later in the year.

event: India cuts fuel excise, raises export duties
description: India reduced excise duties on petrol and diesel by ₹10 per litre to keep domestic fuel prices from rising, while raising export duties to ₹21.5/litre on diesel and ₹29.5/litre on aviation fuel to protect domestic supply.

event: NZ launches four-level fuel alert system
description: New Zealand released a four-level fuel alert system in response to shortages; the country was placed on the first phase, 'watchful'.
British supermarket chain Asda warned it was already facing 'temporary shortages' at some of its petrol pumps.

event: Analysts warn of a decisive new oil shock
description: Analysts warned that another hard oil crisis was unfolding that would be very decisive for the global economy.
Gasoline prices surpassed $6 a gallon in seven California counties as of 30 March.

event: Mauritius down to 21 days of fuel stock
description: A scheduled oil shipment failed to arrive on 30 March, leaving Mauritius with only 21 days of fuel stock; government arranged more expensive alternative fuel shipped from Singapore.

event: Australia announces National Fuel Security Plan
description: Following a National Cabinet meeting, the Australian Government announced a National Fuel Security Plan, moving the country to level two ('Keeping Australia moving'); federal government cut the fuel excise by 50% and paused road user charges for trucks for three months.
Asian countries ramped up use of coal and other 'dirty fuels' to cover the energy shortfall triggered by the Iran war.
All shopping centres and commercial establishments in Bangladesh were directed to shut by 8pm to conserve fuel and power (later revised to 6pm, then 7pm).

event: India: 580,000 new piped-gas connections in March
description: India installed piped gas connections to 580,000 new households in March 2026, as the LPG import crisis pushed a shift toward domestically-sourced piped gas.
Australia, which sources most of its jet fuel from China, followed by Singapore and South Korea, holds 30 days' worth of jet fuel in reserve.

event: Thailand: 57 million litres of fuel missing at sea
description: Thailand's Minister of Justice announced that 57 million litres of fuel were found missing from 217 million litres transported by sea to six oil depots in Surat Thani province; only 160 million litres arrived.
Gas prices in Canada rose approximately 30 percent from March to April.

Bangchak Corporation announced a program letting customers exchange 2 litres of used cooking oil for 1 litre of diesel or petrol (up to 20 litres per person), at 15 stations in the Bangkok Metropolitan Region, effective 6-30 April.

event: Thai diesel price peaks at 50.54 THB/litre
description: Thailand's diesel price reached a peak of 50.54 Thai Baht per litre on 7 April, up from 29.94 THB/litre in February.

event: JPMorgan warns US gas could hit $5/gallon
description: US gas prices had risen $1.16 a gallon since the start of the war; JPMorgan analysts warned prices could breach $5/gallon if the Strait of Hormuz remained shut by mid-April.

event: US consumers hit with fuel surcharges
description: Jet fuel in North America spiked 95% since the war began; USPS, Amazon and FedEx implemented fuel surcharges; airlines raised checked-baggage fees.

A series of protests against rising fuel prices began across major road networks, cities and ports in the Republic of Ireland; protests continued until 14 April and resulted in a vote of no confidence in the government.
Iran and the United States announced a ceasefire. Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained far below pre-war levels even after the announcement.
Thailand's Energy Policy Administration Committee announced a refinery-level diesel price cut of 2 THB/litre effective 9 April, dropping the price from 50.54 to 48.40 THB/litre.
Ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained significantly lower than pre-war levels despite the ceasefire.
Over 180,000 tonnes of fuel went undelivered in recent weeks, halving Ethiopia's daily diesel supply from 9.2 million to 4.5 million litres, according to Minister Kassahun Gofe.

event: Jet fuel crunch warning at European airports
description: Airports were warned they could face a jet fuel crunch within three weeks as airlines weighed flight cancellations.
Normal diesel prices dropped to 44.40 THB/litre and Diesel B20 to 37.40 THB/litre.
The German government announced tax cuts for petrol and diesel fuel for two months in response to rising prices.

event: IEA April Oil Market Report published
description: Global oil supply plummeted 10.1 mb/d to 97 mb/d in March, the largest disruption in history; OPEC+ production fell 9.4 mb/d m-o-m to 42.4 mb/d. North Sea Dated crude traded around $130/bbl, $60/bbl above pre-conflict levels. Oil demand forecast cut to a contraction of 80 kb/d for 2026.

event: Kenya fuel prices hit record high
description: Kenya's Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) announced record high fuel price increases.
Public transport operators (matatus and boda bodas) hiked fares by roughly 25% following the fuel price increase.

event: NYT: why gas prices are slow to fall
description: Analysis of US retail gasoline pricing dynamics (AAA national average data) during the crisis, on why prices rise fast and fall slowly.

event: IEA: Middle East crisis disrupts gas markets
description: IEA reported that Middle East disruptions had tightened global gas balances and delayed the global LNG supply wave, with the market projected to stay tight through 2026-2027.
US exports of crude and petroleum products rose to nearly 12.9 million barrels a day.

event: ECB and BOE hold interest rates
description: The European Central Bank and the Bank of England left interest rates unchanged, citing uncertainty over the fate of the Strait of Hormuz.
Spirit Airlines ceased all operations, citing rising fuel costs, despite the Trump administration's attempts to save the company.
War-driven energy shortages gave China an opportunity to expand its regional influence in Asia, including via limited refined-product exports to select partner countries.

event: IEA May Oil Market Report published
description: Global oil supply declined a further 1.8 mb/d in April to 95.1 mb/d, taking total losses since February to 12.8 mb/d; Gulf output was 14.4 mb/d below pre-war levels. North Sea Dated averaged $120.36/bbl in April, up ~$16.50/bbl month-on-month.

IEA projected total 2026 energy investment of $3.4 trillion: oil investment falling for a third consecutive year to below $500 billion; natural gas investment rising to $330 billion (highest in a decade); coal investment reaching $180 billion (highest since 2012). IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol described the crisis as 'the largest energy security crisis the world has ever faced'.

event: Vox: how China is keeping down oil prices
description: Analysis of how China's reduced crude buying has helped keep down world oil prices during the crisis.

event: NYT: China's leverage over the oil price
description: Analysis of how China's purchasing decisions can move the world oil price even without buying more.
By late June 2026, China's strategic petroleum reserve remained nearly unchanged after the Iran war; to preserve it, China halted supplies of refined oil products to other countries.
